cross_item_review.shared_solve_procedure: Identify the speaker and addressee for each quoted pronoun, then assign the action and possessed object to those people.
cross_item_review.format_repetition: Both use two named people, future proposals, possessive pronouns, and four complete role-map choices; this creates a recognizable surface pattern.
cross_item_review.mechanism_difference: PR-01 keeps one speaker while mapping two reciprocal actions and two possessions across one sentence. PR-02 changes speakers between turns and asks the learner to track 'my' after that shift, with an offer rather than a second action plan.
cross_item_review.scaling_concern_for_20_item_mixed_bank: These two can coexist, but many more two-person I/you/my/your questions with the same four full-sentence role maps would become formulaic. Vary dialogue structures, the number and placement of referents, and the decision the learner must make while keeping each referent unambiguous.
